source.anchor_kjv: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.
source.thread: Psalm 22 closes on 'that he hath done this' and Jesus' last breath in John is 'It is finished' - the same finished work, a thousand years apart
source.hook_line: A psalm's last line and Jesus' last breath in John close on the very same note: it is done.
source.spoken_script: A psalm's last line and Jesus' last breath in John close on the very same note: it is done. The psalm closes looking ahead to God's saving work, accomplished, and told to a people not yet born. Its final line: " that he hath done this." Done. And as Jesus hung dying, John records His final word: "It is finished". Different words, in different tongues, a thousand years apart but the same note: a finished work. So what's left for you to finish? Nothing only Someone to come home to: the One who said it is done.

platforms.description:
A psalm's last line and Jesus' last breath close on the very same note (Psalm 22:31; John 19:30).

"They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this" (Psalm 22:31, KJV).

The psalm ends looking ahead to God's saving work, accomplished, and told to a people not yet born. Its final line: he hath done this. Done. And as Jesus hung dying, John records his final word: "It is finished" (John 19:30). Different words, in different tongues, a thousand years apart, but the same note: a finished work.

So what is left for you to finish? Nothing. Only Someone to come home to: the One who said it is done.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: He Hath Done This: How Psalm 22 Ends Where Jesus Ends
platforms.description:
Psalm 22 begins with the forsaken cry Jesus prayed from the cross. Its very last line looks ahead to a saving work already accomplished, declared to a people not yet born (Psalm 22:31; John 19:30).

"They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this" (Psalm 22:31, KJV).

And as Jesus hung dying, John records his final word: "It is finished" (John 19:30). Different words, in different tongues, a thousand years apart, but the same note: a finished work. The psalm that opened in abandonment closes in accomplishment, and the man who prayed its first line breathed its last.

So what is left for you to finish? Nothing. Only Someone to come home to: the One who said it is done.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- KJV check: Psalm 22:31 quoted verbatim as supplied and front-loaded in YT/FB; "It is finished" is verbatim John 19:30 and correctly attributed to John's account (important, since Luke records a different final saying - the kit never claims otherwise). PASS.
- Honesty check: the kit mirrors the video's own care ("Different words, in different tongues... the same note") and never claims the two endings are the same sentence. No overclaim.
- youtube_long block only (not rendered for a short unit): "the man who prayed its first line breathed its last" is a garbled construction - it reads as the idiom "breathed his last" misapplied to the psalm. If this block is ever used for a real long-form, rewrite to "and the man who prayed its first line ended where the psalm ends: it is done." Non-blocking here because the short pack renders only the four short platform files.
- instagram (minor, non-blocking): "Jesus' last breath: It is finished" compresses away the "John records" attribution the other platforms keep. Acceptable at caption length; the video itself supplies the attribution.
- Titles: chosen title is specific and true; no collision with the sibling piece titled "It Is Finished" (it_is_finished_john1930) - the shared #ItIsFinished hashtag is fine, titles differ.
- Grace check: "Nothing left for you to finish, only Someone to come home to" is grace-anchored invitation, no fear or gain-loss framing. PASS.
